_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Madagascar covering Austronesian settlement (unique in Africa), Merina kingdom, French colonisation, 1947 uprising, independence, Ratsiraka socialism, political crises, and world-renowned biodiversity including lemurs.

ethnic_groups.name: Merina (Imerina)
ethnic_groups.notes: Central Highlands; Antananarivo; Austronesian; historically royal and politically dominant; rice terraces; andriana noble class

ethnic_groups.name: Betsimisaraka
ethnic_groups.notes: Eastern coast; second-largest group; mixed Austronesian-Bantu; 'the many inseparable'

ethnic_groups.name: Betsileo
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern central highlands; Austronesian; skilled rice farmers; Fianarantsoa region

ethnic_groups.name: Tsimihety
ethnic_groups.notes: North-central; 'those who do not cut their hair'; historically resisted Merina rule

ethnic_groups.name: Sakalava
ethnic_groups.notes: Western coast; Menabe and Boina kingdoms; Austronesian; distinct royal traditions

ethnic_groups.name: Antaisaka
ethnic_groups.notes: Southeastern coast; paper-making tradition from Antemoro influence

ethnic_groups.name: Antandroy
ethnic_groups.notes: Deep South; semi-arid; 'people of thorns'; zebu cattle herders; drought-prone

ethnic_groups.name: Antankarana
ethnic_groups.notes: Far north; Diego Suarez (Antsiranana); mixed Sakalava-Swahili heritage

ethnic_groups.name: Bara
ethnic_groups.notes: Southern plateau; zebu cattle culture; pastoralists

ethnic_groups.name: Antemoro
ethnic_groups.notes: Southeastern coast; Islamic heritage; Sorabe Arabic script; paper-making

ethnic_groups.name: Mahafaly
ethnic_groups.notes: Southwest; aloalo funerary posts; zebu sacrifice traditions

ethnic_groups.name: Vezo
ethnic_groups.notes: Western and southern coasts; 'people of the sea'; fishing culture

ethnic_groups.name: Other (18+ groups)
ethnic_groups.notes: Bezanozano, Sihanaka, Tanala, Antanosy, Makoa (Bantu from Mozambique), Karana (Indo-Pakistani), Chinese, French, Comorian

country_profile.notes_unique: World's fourth-largest island; over 90% of its wildlife is found nowhere else on Earth; Austronesian origins link its language and culture to Southeast Asia.

natural_resources.notes: World's largest vanilla producer (~80% of global supply); Ambatovy nickel/cobalt mine (one of largest in world); ilmenite mining at Fort Dauphin; massive sapphire deposits; unique biodiversity (90% endemic species) is itself a resource via ecotourism.

military.notes: People's Armed Forces; historically involved in politics (2009 coup); gendarmerie handles most rural security; limited naval capacity despite enormous maritime zone.

debt_aid.notes: HIPC debt relief; heavily aid-dependent; France, World Bank, AfDB major donors; political instability deters investment; vanilla price volatility affects economy.

education.notes: Education quality declining; many children drop out by secondary level; language of instruction debates (Malagasy vs French); teacher absenteeism; private schooling growing in cities.

diaspora_migration.notes: French diaspora largest community; relatively low outmigration given population size; internal rural-urban migration significant.

digital_economy.notes: METISS submarine cable improved connectivity; mobile money expanding rapidly; BPO/call centre industry serving French market; Telma, Orange, Airtel operators.

current_leader.name: Andry Rajoelina
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: Former mayor of Antananarivo; ousted Ravalomanana in 2009 coup; returned via 2018 election; re-elected 2023; businessman

former_leaders.name: Philibert Tsiranana
former_leaders.notes: First president; pro-French; PSD party; overthrown in 1972 protests

former_leaders.name: Didier Ratsiraka
former_leaders.notes: Admiral; socialist Malagasy Revolution; DidiVision TV addresses; economic collapse; returned 1997; fled to France 2002

former_leaders.name: Marc Ravalomanana
former_leaders.notes: Self-made dairy tycoon (Tiko); modernization; 2009 crisis and military ouster; exile in South Africa

910.name: Austronesian Settlement of Madagascar
910.description: Madagascar's unique Austronesian settlement — one of the great maritime migrations, arriving from Borneo across the Indian Ocean; mixed Bantu and Austronesian heritage.

sub_clusters.name: Austronesian Voyagers from Borneo
sub_clusters.description: Outrigger canoe voyages from Southeast Asia (Borneo) across 5,000+ km of Indian Ocean; linguistic and genetic evidence ties Malagasy to Ma'anyan language.

sub_clusters.name: Bantu and Arab Arrivals
sub_clusters.description: Bantu-speaking Africans from East African coast arrive; Arab and Indian traders establish presence; cultural synthesis creates distinct Malagasy identity.

sub_clusters.name: Megafauna Extinction
sub_clusters.description: Human arrival triggers extinction of giant lemurs, elephant birds (Aepyornis), and dwarf hippos; deforestation and hunting.

920.name: Early Malagasy Kingdoms and Chiefdoms
920.description: Rise of regional kingdoms and chiefdoms; Sakalava empire; Antemoro literate class; Indian Ocean trade networks.

sub_clusters.name: Sakalava Empire
sub_clusters.description: Sakalava (Menabe and Boina) establish western Madagascar's largest pre-colonial state; cattle wealth; slave raiding across the Mozambique Channel.

sub_clusters.name: Antemoro and Sorabe Manuscripts
sub_clusters.description: Antemoro (claimed Arab descent) develop Sorabe script — Malagasy written in Arabic characters; unique literary tradition in sub-Saharan Africa.

sub_clusters.name: Pirate Haven of Madagascar
sub_clusters.description: Madagascar as base for Indian Ocean pirates; Île Sainte-Marie; legends of Libertalia; mixed-race Zana-Malata communities.

930.name: Merina Kingdom and Unification
930.description: Highland Merina kingdom unifies much of Madagascar; Andrianampoinimerina and Radama I; London Missionary Society; Ranavalona I's isolationist reign.

sub_clusters.name: Andrianampoinimerina's Unification
sub_clusters.description: King Andrianampoinimerina unifies the Merina highlands; 'The sea is the limit of my rice paddy'; builds administrative infrastructure.

sub_clusters.name: Radama I and Modernisation
sub_clusters.description: Radama I allies with Britain; abolishes external slave trade; London Missionary Society introduces Christianity and Latin script; modernised army conquers most of Madagascar.

sub_clusters.name: Ranavalona I and Isolationism
sub_clusters.description: Queen Ranavalona I expels foreigners and persecutes Christians; reasserts traditional practices; controversial but symbolises resistance to European influence.

sub_clusters.name: Franco-Merina Wars
sub_clusters.description: First (1883-85) and Second (1894-96) Franco-Merina Wars; French conquest; Queen Ranavalona III exiled; Madagascar becomes French colony 1897.

940.name: French Colonial Madagascar
940.description: French colonial rule under Gallieni; forced labour; 1947 uprising; evolving nationalist movement.

sub_clusters.name: Gallieni and Colonial Pacification
sub_clusters.description: Governor Gallieni's politique des races; abolition of Merina monarchy and aristocratic privileges; construction of colonial infrastructure; forced labour.

sub_clusters.name: 1947 Malagasy Uprising
sub_clusters.description: Major anti-colonial revolt in eastern Madagascar March 1947; brutal French suppression kills estimated 11,000-89,000; MDRM leaders sentenced.

sub_clusters.name: Road to Independence
sub_clusters.description: Loi-cadre reforms 1956; Philibert Tsiranana's PSD; autonomy within French Community 1958; full independence 26 June 1960.

950.name: First Republic and Ratsiraka Socialism
950.description: Tsiranana's First Republic; 1972 revolution; Didier Ratsiraka's socialist Second Republic; economic decline.

sub_clusters.name: Tsiranana's First Republic
sub_clusters.description: Independence under Philibert Tsiranana; continued French influence; neo-colonial economy; 1971-72 peasant revolts in the south.

sub_clusters.name: 1972 Revolution and Military Rule
sub_clusters.description: Student and worker protests topple Tsiranana; General Ramanantsoa leads transition; instability; Ratsiraka takes power 1975.

sub_clusters.name: Ratsiraka's Socialist Experiment
sub_clusters.description: Didier Ratsiraka's Charter of the Malagasy Socialist Revolution; nationalisation; economic collapse; diplomatic non-alignment; opposition grows by late 1980s.

960.name: Democratic Madagascar and Political Crises
960.description: Democratic transition; recurring political crises and unconstitutional changes of government; biodiversity conservation efforts.

sub_clusters.name: Third Republic and Zafy-Ratsiraka Rivalry
sub_clusters.description: Albert Zafy's Third Republic 1993; impeachment 1996; Ratsiraka returns 1997; contested 2001 election sparks crisis.

sub_clusters.name: Ravalomanana Presidency
sub_clusters.description: Marc Ravalomanana consolidates power after 2001-02 crisis; economic growth; Daewoo land deal controversy; overthrown 2009.

sub_clusters.name: 2009 Crisis and Rajoelina Transition
sub_clusters.description: Andry Rajoelina seizes power in 2009 coup; international condemnation; SADC mediation; return to elections 2013.

sub_clusters.name: Biodiversity and Environmental Challenges
sub_clusters.description: Madagascar as mega-biodiversity hotspot; 90% species endemism; lemurs; deforestation crisis; rosewood trafficking; conservation NGOs.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
